message.content:
Idea-stage product spec for a Nxeon "backup upsell" — the user wants to upsell customers on backup FREQUENCY and STORAGE across all services (VPS, game servers, shared hosting). Read-only; do NOT modify the repo. Produce ONE markdown spec at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/ideas/backup-upsell-spec.md (create the dir).

Study what backup capability already exists so the spec builds on reality, not greenfield:
- VPS backups: lib/proxmox.ts (listBackups / snapshot / backup), the Snapshots/Backups tabs in app/dashboard/servers/[id], worker backup timers (systemd nxeon-backup-* per the timers list).
- Shared hosting backups: worker/hosting.ts taskBackup (tar + mysqldump, retain newest 5), the Backups panel.
- Any existing billing add-on pattern: lib/actions.ts (disk expand / volume pricing), coupons, the wallet/billing model — how a recurring paid add-on is modeled today (grep for extra_disk / volume_price / add-on).

The spec should define:
1. **The offer**: backup frequency tiers (e.g. free = weekly/manual, paid = daily, premium = hourly) and retention/storage tiers (keep N backups / X GB of backup storage), per service.
2. **Pricing** (recurring add-on $/mo) benchmarked against competitors, and where it appears in the funnel (at order, and as an upsell in the server/account panel).
3. **Schema sketch** (a BackupPlan / BackupAddon model or fields on the subscription) and how it plugs into the existing billing/renewal worker.
4. **Enforcement**: how the worker reads the tier to set backup cadence + retention (cron cadence, retention count, off-node storage for the premium tier).
5. **MVP vs full**: the smallest version that's sellable (e.g. just a "daily backups" toggle add-on on VPS) → the full cross-service matrix.
Be concrete + reference the existing code paths so implementation is a straight follow-up.

content.thinking:
I'm seeing the VPS backup architecture now—there's a boolean flag for auto-backups, an interval setting in hours, and a timestamp tracking the last backup. A scheduler worker periodically checks if a backup is due and queues backup jobs, which then trigger the vzdump utility to run.

The system keeps only 2 backups per customer by default through a pruning function that's already parameterized for the keep count. There's also an offsite backup timer at the platform level. Currently, daily auto-backups are offered as a free included feature in the deployment wizard with a 24-hour interval.

For shared hosting, backups work differently—they're manually triggered tasks that tar the home directory and dump the database, keeping the 5 most recent copies. The add-on billing model follows the pattern of extra disk storage, which has a configurable price per GB per month and gets charged at order time with prorated amounts, then renewed monthly through the billing sweep worker.

The renewal system splits across products: VPS renewals go through the main billing sweep with a prices object carrying all the add-on rates, while email, hosting, and volume products have their own renewal workers that calculate charges based on the specific plan or product type. input.content:
# Nxeon Backup Upsell — Product Spec (idea stage)

Upsell customers on backup **frequency** and **retention/storage** across all services
(VPS, game servers, shared hosting). This spec builds on the backup machinery that
already ships — it is not greenfield. Every section names the exact file/field a
follow-up would touch.

---

## 0. What already exists (ground truth)

### VPS + game servers (same `Server` table)
Game servers are just `Server` rows with `gamePlanId` set, so they run through the
**identical** Proxmox backup path — no separate mechanism needed.

- **Schema** — `prisma/schema.prisma` `model Server` (line ~316):
  - `autoBackup Boolean @default(false)`
  - `backupIntervalHours Int?`  — the scheduled cadence
  - `lastAutoBackup DateTime?`  — set only when an archive is **observed** in storage
    (not at enqueue; this is the fix for incident H4)
- **Scheduler** — `worker/backup-schedule.ts` `scheduledBackupSweep()`: finds
  `status:RUNNING, autoBackup:true, backupIntervalHours != null`, checks
  `lib/backup-verify.ts isAutoBackupDue()`, enqueues one `BACKUP_CREATE` job
  (de-duped on in-flight jobs).
- **Executor** — `worker/index.ts` `backupCreate(job)` (line ~903): runs `vzdump`,
  then prunes via `lib/proxmox.ts pruneBackups(conn, vmid, keep)`. Retention is the
  **hardcoded constant** `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP = 2` (worker/index.ts line ~49).
  `pruneBackups(client, vmid, keep)` already takes `keep` as a parameter — it just
  isn't sourced per-customer yet. **This is the single lever for the retention tier.**
- **Proxmox lib** — `lib/proxmox.ts`: `listBackups`, `listBackupsOn`, `deleteBackup`,
  `pruneBackups`, `backupDumpDir`. Whole-system/offsite archives are separate and
  platform-level (`scripts/backup-vms.sh`, `scripts/backup-offsite.sh`,
  `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer`) — **not** per-customer today.

### Shared hosting (`HostingAccount`)
- **Executor** — `worker/hosting.ts` `taskBackup()` (line ~805): `mysqldump` of the
  account's `<user>_%` DBs + `tar` of the home tree → one `.tar.gz` under
  `/var/hosting-backups/<user>/`. Writes a `HostingBackup` row, then **retains newest
  5** (`all.slice(5)` → delete). Hardcoded.
- **Trigger** — `HostingTask` kind `BACKUP` (enum in schema). **Manual only today** —
  there is **no cadence field** on `HostingAccount` and no scheduled hosting-backup
  sweep. Cadence + auto-scheduling is net-new for hosting.
- **Schema** — `model HostingBackup { accountId, path, sizeBytes, createdAt }`.

### Existing recurring paid add-on pattern (the template to copy)
The gold-standard model is **extra disk**, mirrored by dedicated IP / volumes / email:

| Add-on | Field / model | Price source (admin setting) | Renewal fold-in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Extra disk | `Server.extraDiskGB` | `extra_disk_gb_price_cents` (default 10 = $0.10/GB/mo) | `lib/renewal-charge.ts` |
| Dedicated IP | `Server.dedicatedIp` | `dedicated_ip_price_cents` | `lib/renewal-charge.ts` |
| Volume | `Volume` rows | `volume_price_cents_per_gb` (10) | `volumeRenewalCents` |
| Email plan | `EmailSubscription` | `emailRenewalCents(plan)` | `worker/product-renewals.ts` |

- **Charged at order** through the ONE quote path: `lib/order.ts intentFromFormData →
  orderQuote → placeOrder`. Extra disk gets its own invoice line item.
- **Renews** through `worker/billing.ts billingSweep()` → `lib/renewal-charge.ts
  renewalCharge(server, prices)`, where `prices = { ipMonthlyCents, extraDiskPerGbCents }`.
  **This `prices` object is exactly where a backup add-on price folds in.**
- **Display === charge invariant is sacred** (2026-07-25 incident): `lib/renewal-quote.ts`
  mirrors `renewal-charge.ts` so the customer sees the real number. Any backup add-on
  MUST flow through these two files together, never a second recomputation.

### The trap this spec must avoid (learn from the existing bug)
`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` sells **"Daily auto-backups"** (currently tagged
**"Included"** / free) via hidden input `addon_backup`. That flag was once *write-only*:
it landed in `Server.addons.dailyBackup` but the scheduler keys off
`autoBackup`+`backupIntervalHours`, so every server carried the promise with
`autoBackup:false` and **no backup ever ran**. `lib/order.ts` (line ~520) now bridges
it: `autoBackup = !!intent.addonBackup; backupIntervalHours = 24`. **Any new tier field
must bridge to the columns the scheduler actually reads, or it will silently sell air.**

---

## 1. The offer

Two independent axes, exactly as requested: **frequency** and **retention/storage**.
Baseline stays free so **no existing customer is downgraded** (today's product already
promises free daily backups; we upsell *around* that, never take it away).

### Frequency tiers (flat $/mo)
| Tier | VPS / Game cadence (`backupIntervalHours`) | Shared hosting cadence |
|---|---|---|
| **Free / Standard** (included) | Daily (24h) | Manual / weekly |
| **Plus** | Twice daily (12h) | Daily |
| **Pro** | Every 6h | Every 6–12h |

> Honesty note: full `vzdump` of a whole VM is heavy — true "hourly" full archives are
> not realistic and would thrash the node. The premium *frequency* ceiling is ~6h for
> full archives. If sub-hourly restore points are wanted, that's a **snapshot** product
> (the Snapshots tab / `pve .../snapshot`), which is cheap and instant — sell "frequent
> restore points" as snapshots, "durable copies" as vzdump archives. Keep the two
> distinct in copy so we never over-promise.

### Retention / storage tiers
Model this as **keep-N** for MVP (one integer, one line of code) and optionally graduate
to **metered GB** for the full build (mirrors extra-disk/snapshot pricing).

| Tier | Keep N archives (VPS) | Keep N (hosting) | Storage location |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | 2 (current `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP`) | 5 (current `taskBackup`) | On-node |
| **Plus** | 7 (a week) | 14 | On-node |
| **Pro** | 14 | 30 | On-node |
| **Premium** | 30 | 30 | **+ off-node/offsite copy** |

Premium's differentiator is **off-node durability** (survives a node-loss), which is the
one thing the free on-node tier cannot promise. This is net-new capability — see §4.

---

## 2. Pricing & funnel placement

### Competitor benchmark
- **DigitalOcean / Vultr**: auto-backups = **20% of the plan price/mo** (weekly). Snapshots
  ~$0.05–0.06/GB/mo.
- **Linode/Akamai**: flat **$2–$5/mo** by plan size (Nanode $2 → larger up to ~$20).
- **Hostinger** (our clone target): daily backups bundled on higher tiers, weekly on entry;
  restore is the upsell hook.
- **cPanel shared hosts (JetBackup)**: often $1–3/mo or bundled.

### Proposed Nxeon prices (recurring add-on, admin-tunable settings)
Flat tiers are simpler to sell and to reason about than percent-of-plan, and match the
existing flat-add-on style (dedicated IP, extra disk). Anchor low to look generous next to
DO's 20%:

| Tier | VPS / Game $/mo | Shared hosting $/mo |
|---|---|---|
| Free / Standard | $0 | $0 |
| Plus (7 keep / 12h) | **$2.99** | **$1.49** |
| Pro (14 keep / 6h) | **$4.99** | **$2.99** |
| Premium (30 keep / offsite) | **$8.99** | **$4.99** |

Optional **metered storage** overage for the full build: `$0.05/GB/mo` of backup storage
beyond the tier's included allowance (benchmarked to DO snapshot $0.06). Setting key
`backup_storage_gb_price_cents` (default 5).

All prices live in admin settings so they're tunable without a deploy, following
`extra_disk_gb_price_cents`:
- `backup_plus_price_cents` (default 299)
- `backup_pro_price_cents` (default 499)
- `backup_premium_price_cents` (default 899)
- (hosting variants) `hosting_backup_plus_price_cents`, `..._pro_...`, `..._premium_...`
- `backup_storage_gb_price_cents` (default 5) — full build only

### Where it appears in the funnel
1. **At order** — `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`. Replace the single
   "Daily auto-backups — Included" toggle with a small tier picker
   (Free / Plus / Pro / Premium). Emits `backup_tier` instead of/alongside `addon_backup`.
   Priced through `orderQuote` so it shows as its own invoice line (copy the extra-disk
   line-item pattern in `lib/order.ts`).
2. **Post-purchase upsell** — the **Backups tab** in
   `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` (and the hosting Backups panel). A "Protect this
   server better" card: shows current tier + a one-click upgrade that prorates the
   remaining term (copy `lib/disk-expand.ts diskExpandQuote/applyDiskExpand` — it already
   does prorated mid-term add-on upgrades against the wallet).
3. **Renewal warning** — `worker/billing.ts` already emits "renews soon"; the backup
   line rides along in `renewalCharge` totals automatically once wired.

---

## 3. Schema sketch

Prefer **fields on the existing rows** over a separate model — it matches how every other
add-on is stored (extraDiskGB, dedicatedIp) and keeps `renewalCharge` a pure function of
the row.

```prisma
// Shared enum
enum BackupTier { FREE PLUS PRO PREMIUM }

model Server {
  // ...existing autoBackup / backupIntervalHours / lastAutoBackup...
  backupTier   BackupTier @default(FREE)   // NEW — drives cadence + retention + price
  backupKeep   Int?                        // NEW — resolved retention (nullable => tier default)
  backupOffsite Boolean   @default(false)  // NEW — Premium off-node copy
}

model HostingAccount {
  // ...existing...
  backupTier          BackupTier @default(FREE) // NEW
  backupIntervalHours Int?                       // NEW — hosting had NO cadence field before
  backupKeep          Int?                       // NEW
  lastAutoBackup      DateTime?                  // NEW — mirror the Server semantics
  backupOffsite       Boolean    @default(false) // NEW
}
```

`backupTier` is the single source of truth sold + charged; `backupIntervalHours` /
`backupKeep` / `backupOffsite` are the **resolved** enforcement values (so an admin can
tune the tier→values mapping centrally without a migration). A tiny resolver —
`lib/backup-tiers.ts backupTierSpec(tier)` returning
`{ intervalHours, keep, offsite, priceCents }` — is the one place cadence/retention/price
per tier is defined, consumed by both the scheduler and the pricer.

**Alternative** (only if backups must be sold à-la-carte or transferred between services):
a `BackupAddon { id, ownerType, ownerId, tier, priceCents, createdAt }` model. Heavier;
not recommended for MVP.

### Billing wiring
- Add `backupMonthlyCents` to the `prices` object in `worker/billing.ts billingSweep` and
  thread it into `lib/renewal-charge.ts renewalCharge()` + `lib/renewal-quote.ts`
  (edit them **together** — that pairing is the display===charge guard). It slots beside
  `extraDiskCents` as another add-on line in `totalCents`.
- Order-time: extend `lib/order.ts intentFromFormData` with `backupTier`, price it in
  `orderQuote`, add its invoice line in `placeOrder` (copy the `extraDiskCents` block).
- **Bridge, don't sell air**: in `placeOrder`, set
  `autoBackup = tier != FREE || currentDefault`, `backupIntervalHours = spec.intervalHours`,
  `backupKeep = spec.keep`, `backupOffsite = spec.offsite` — the columns the scheduler
  reads — right where the current `addonBackup` bridge lives.
- Hosting renewal: `worker/product-renewals.ts chargeHostingRenewal` adds a backup line
  the same way (`hosting_backup_*_price_cents`).

---

## 4. Enforcement (worker reads the tier)

### VPS / game — minimal changes, machinery already exists
1. **Cadence**: `worker/backup-schedule.ts scheduledBackupSweep` already keys off
   `backupIntervalHours`. Just ensure the resolver stamps
   `backupIntervalHours = backupTierSpec(server.backupTier).intervalHours` at order and on
   any tier change (and keep `isAutoBackupDue` as-is).
2. **Retention**: replace the constant in `worker/index.ts backupCreate`:
   ```
   const keep = server.backupKeep ?? backupTierSpec(server.backupTier).keep; // was CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP
   await pruneBackups(conn, vmid, keep);
   ```
   `pruneBackups(client, vmid, keep)` already accepts `keep` — **one-line change**.
3. **Off-node (Premium only)**: after a successful `vzdump`, if `server.backupOffsite`,
   copy the archive to the offsite target. Reuse the mechanism in
   `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` / the `nxeon-backup-offsite` service, but scoped to a single
   `vmid` archive rather than the whole-system dump. This is the **one genuinely new
   capability** and the main build cost of Premium. Track the offsite copy so restore can
   find it (either a `location` column on a per-archive record, or a naming convention the
   `listBackupsOn` filter recognizes).

### Shared hosting — needs a new sweep (net-new)
`taskBackup` runs, but nothing schedules it on a cadence. Add:
1. A hosting equivalent of `scheduledBackupSweep` (or a phase inside
   `worker/product-renewals.ts` / the hosting worker loop): find `ACTIVE` accounts with
   `backupTier != FREE` whose `lastAutoBackup` is older than `backupIntervalHours`, enqueue
   a `HostingTask` kind `BACKUP`.
2. Parameterize retention in `taskBackup`: replace `all.slice(5)` with
   `all.slice(account.backupKeep ?? backupTierSpec(account.backupTier).keep)`.
3. Premium offsite: `scp`/`rclone` the `.tar.gz` off the node after write.

Enforcement rule of thumb: **tier → resolver → the two knobs (`intervalHours`, `keep`)
+ the offsite flag.** No enforcement logic branches on `backupTier` directly except the
resolver.

---

## 5. MVP vs full

### MVP (smallest sellable slice — VPS/game only, ~a day of work)
- Sell one **paid daily-retention upgrade** on VPS/game: Free (keep 2) → **Plus (keep 7)**
  for a flat `$2.99/mo`. Frequency stays daily for everyone; **retention is the only knob**.
- Schema: `Server.backupTier` + `Server.backupKeep` (skip offsite for now).
- Enforcement: the **one-line** `pruneBackups` change in `worker/index.ts` reading
  `backupKeep`. That's the entire enforcement surface — cadence is untouched.
- Billing: thread `backupMonthlyCents` through `renewal-charge.ts` + `renewal-quote.ts`,
  add the order line in `lib/order.ts`, add the settings key.
- Funnel: DeployWizard toggle → tier picker; a "Keep more restore points" upgrade card on
  the Backups tab using the existing `disk-expand` prorate flow.
- Ships value on day one because the retention lever (`pruneBackups(keep)`) and the
  renewal pipeline both already exist.

### Full (cross-service matrix)
- **Frequency tiers** on VPS/game (12h / 6h) via `backupIntervalHours` from the resolver.
- **Shared hosting** brought in: new cadence field + scheduled BACKUP sweep + parameterized
  retention in `taskBackup`.
- **Premium off-node storage** for both services (the real durability sell) — the main new
  engineering.
- **Metered GB overage** (`backup_storage_gb_price_cents`) for customers who exceed the
  tier's included allowance, priced like snapshots/extra-disk.
- **Game servers**: decide the pricing model — `renewalCharge`'s `isGame` branch is
  currently *flat all-in with no add-on lines*, so either (a) fold a flat backup surcharge
  into that branch, or (b) roll backup tiers into the `GamePlan` price. MVP simply leaves
  game on Free until this is decided.

---

## Key file/field index (for the implementer)
- Tiers/cadence/retention/price mapping (NEW): `lib/backup-tiers.ts`
- VPS schema: `prisma/schema.prisma` `model Server` (~316) — add `backupTier/backupKeep/backupOffsite`
- Hosting schema: `model HostingAccount` (~812) — add `backupTier/backupIntervalHours/backupKeep/lastAutoBackup/backupOffsite`
- Retention lever (VPS): `worker/index.ts` `backupCreate` + `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP` (~49) → read `backupKeep`
- Retention lever (hosting): `worker/hosting.ts` `taskBackup` `all.slice(5)` → read `backupKeep`
- Cadence scheduler (VPS): `worker/backup-schedule.ts` `scheduledBackupSweep` (already reads `backupIntervalHours`)
- Cadence scheduler (hosting): NEW sweep alongside `worker/product-renewals.ts`
- Prune primitive: `lib/proxmox.ts` `pruneBackups(client, vmid, keep)` (already parameterized)
- Order-time price + bridge: `lib/order.ts` `intentFromFormData/orderQuote/placeOrder` (copy `extraDiskCents` + the `addonBackup`→columns bridge at ~520)
- Renewal price (VPS): `lib/renewal-charge.ts` + `lib/renewal-quote.ts` (edit as a pair) + `prices` object in `worker/billing.ts billingSweep`
- Renewal price (hosting): `worker/product-renewals.ts` `chargeHostingRenewal`
- Mid-term prorated upgrade template: `lib/disk-expand.ts` `diskExpandQuote/applyDiskExpand`
- Funnel UI: `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` (order) + `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` Backups tab (upsell)
- Admin price settings (via `getSettingInt`): `backup_plus_price_cents`, `backup_pro_price_cents`, `backup_premium_price_cents`, hosting variants, `backup_storage_gb_price_cents`

Spec written to `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/ideas/backup-upsell-spec.md`. Repo was not modified (read-only).

## Key findings that shaped the spec

**The backup machinery already exists — this is a wiring/pricing job, not greenfield:**

- **VPS + game servers share one path.** Game servers are just `Server` rows with `gamePlanId` set, so they already flow through the same Proxmox backup. The `Server` model already has `autoBackup`, `backupIntervalHours`, `lastAutoBackup`. The scheduler (`worker/backup-schedule.ts`) reads `backupIntervalHours`; the executor (`worker/index.ts backupCreate`) prunes via `lib/proxmox.ts pruneBackups(conn, vmid, keep)` — which **already takes `keep` as a parameter**, currently pinned to the hardcoded `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP = 2`. Retention enforcement is therefore a **one-line change**.

- **Shared hosting is the gap.** `worker/hosting.ts taskBackup` does tar + mysqldump and retains newest 5 (hardcoded `all.slice(5)`), but it's **manual-trigger only** — `HostingAccount` has no cadence field and there's no scheduled hosting-backup sweep. Auto-scheduling for hosting is the main net-new worker code.

- **There's a proven recurring-add-on pattern to copy: extra disk.** Field on the row (`Server.extraDiskGB`) + admin price setting (`extra_disk_gb_price_cents`) + charged at order via the single `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` path + renewed via `lib/renewal-charge.ts renewalCharge(server, prices)`. The `prices` object is literally where a `backupMonthlyCents` folds in. Dedicated IP, volumes, and email plans all follow this same shape.

- **Two landmines I designed around:** (1) The "displayed === charged" invariant from the 2026-07-25 incident — `renewal-charge.ts` and `renewal-quote.ts` must be edited as a pair. (2) The existing `addons.dailyBackup` was once **write-only** (sold but never bridged to the columns the scheduler reads), so customers paid for backups that never ran — the spec insists any new tier field bridge to `autoBackup`/`backupIntervalHours`/`backupKeep`.

**Offer/pricing design:** two axes (frequency + retention) as requested, with **Free kept at today's daily/keep-2 so no existing customer is downgraded**. Flat tiers (Plus $2.99 / Pro $4.99 / Premium $8.99 on VPS) benchmarked against DO/Vultr's 20%-of-plan and Linode's flat $2–5. Premium's real differentiator is **off-node/offsite storage** — the one genuinely new capability (adaptable from `scripts/backup-offsite.sh`, currently platform-level only).

**MVP** is a single retention upgrade on VPS (Free keep-2 → Plus keep-7, $2.99/mo) — sellable via the one-line `pruneBackups` change plus threading price through the existing renewal pipeline. The full cross-service matrix (frequency tiers, hosting cadence sweep, offsite, metered GB) is staged after.

One open decision flagged for the user: game plans currently use `renewalCharge`'s flat `isGame` branch with **no add-on lines**, so game backups need an explicit pricing decision (flat surcharge vs. rolled into `GamePlan` price) — MVP leaves game on Free.
